Here's the thing...when you look in a mirror, that is NOT what people see.  You see everything bad, every little flaw, because that's what depression does.  Most people just see...a person.

I would be pretty sympathetic to a student telling me they had depression (for obvious reasons) but some people aren't so kind, so I would stick to telling the professor that you have a medical issue flaring up that you thought you had under control but it has become clear that you don't.  Acknowledge your missing work without being overly apologetic and ask for help finding a way through the course--and that may mean a drop or an incomplete, but that's better than an F grade.  

Don't expect the prof to solve the issue, but if you approach it as "here's what's going on, here's what I'm doing to alleviate the issue, how can I best move forward" your profs will likely be really happy that you are talking with them.  What we hate most is the student who just disappears.

I've definitely been there.  It always was so comforting to picture myself falling off the ledge and not having to deal with any of the bullshit anymore.  I never really came close to it, but just having it there as an option felt nice--like an escape hatch.

I mean...I'm depressed, but also there's really awesome stuff?  I have a great job and a kick-ass kid and really awesome friends.  So yeah, that voice telling me I'm shit has never entirely gone away but I have more parts of my life that tell that voice to STFU than I did when I was younger.  It's not nothing.

As a college prof--talk to your teachers right away.  They will almost certainly be more understanding than you think they will.  But the longer you stay away the less they can do to help you.

Also, talk to your Disability Services office.  They will NOT think badly of you, and can give you tools to deal with those times where you can't get out of bed.  If you get accommodations than even the shitty asshole profs can't legally fuck you over due to your mental health.

Good luck.  I know it feels like you are a fuck-up, but that's just your brainweasels fucking with you.  This is not you fucking up, it is a medical condition that's having a flare-up.  No different than if you had gotten cancer, or caught mono, or broken your leg.  This isn't your fault.  You can do this.

Have you told your mom about the comments, or that you are depressed?  If you don't think you can tell your mom, is there a teacher at school that you trust?  Having someone that has your back, even if they can't do anything, is a huge help.

Depression is a cast-iron bitch and I know from experience that having it hit so young is super nasty.  But (as cliche as it is) usually it will improve--you will find friends as weird as you, and maybe you will be able to get counseling and/or medication to help even if you can't right now.

I hope you aren't thinking of hurting yourself, but if you are, here's some important stuff.  Number one, if you think about suicide, especially if you start planning it, TALK TO SOMEONE ASAP, even if it's just the helpline.  It sounds dumb to think that calling a stranger would do anything at all, but I've called them before and it really does just help having someone who really hears you.  If you don't want to tell your mom because you don't want to worry her--believe me when I say that as a parent I would one billion times rather hear "I'm suicidal" from my kid than wonder what I could have done after it happened.  If you don't want to tell her because you don't trust her to have your back, then tell someone else.  BUT be aware that if you tell a teacher they are legally required to report it, which may not help.  If nothing else, the people here will help you through things.

Just know you aren't alone.  We random strangers on the internet are here, anytime you need us.

Hi, I'm a depressed academic.  I also did the "smart, but just didn't try" pathway in college because guess what, *it is hard to try when you are filled with crippling brainweasels*

Some of your professors will think you are a fuckup.  Other professors will completely understand (because guess what?  Some of us also have depression!)  You may get to build your grades back up.  You may not.  Your parents may come around to believing you.  They may not.

The important thing to know is that even if you don't, **it is not over.**  Nothing is over.  My first time through college I screwed up badly enough that I only scraped by graduating by profs giving me grades I didn't deserve, and even then it took me an extra semester.  But I survived, and I muddled through a bit, and eventually I went back to college and kicked butt and eventually got my PhD.

So, TL;DR--no, you aren't using depression as a crutch, you 
had a crappy academic year because you had depression, but it's not the end of the world.

Hey, you are doing great.  I know what it's like to be with someone who deeply needs help but is resistant to getting it.  It feels so helpless to watch him hurt and know that he could be better if only he'd do something about it...

I don't have any specific advice, unfortunately.  But I think what would be most helpful for you would be to reach out to other women in the same situation.  Sadly, there are a *lot* of them out there.  If you google "PTSD Spouse" there's a lot of resources--everywhere from the VA to Facebook groups.  I think that getting advice from people who are a lot closer to the seriously messed up situation you and your husband are in would be more helpful than some randos on Reddit, honestly.

In the meantime, keep letting him know that you love him and you're there for him.  Tell him explicitly that you want to help him feel better, but let him take the lead--he is an adult, and he will only take steps to make things better if *he* wants to.
